title: quantization-debug-notes-int8-nan
content:
Quick debugging breadcrumbs - quantization / precision incident (INT8 / FP8 / BF16)

Context:
- Owner: Jordan Kim (working notes). Not an incident report yet, just breadcrumbs.
- Affects: hosted inference (some model variants) and dedicated pools that use bitsandbytes / GPTQ style quantization.
- Symptoms: intermittent NaNs during inference and evaluation, sometimes catastrophic quality drop (nonsensical generations), sometimes device-side CUDA errors.
- Models tested: small/med LLaMA-like and a 13B open model (fp32 baseline good).

Timeline / quick hits:
- 2025-11-01: first noisy report from QA (Priya) - strange <nan> tokens in outputs after model served with INT8 quant.
- 2025-11-02: repro script (local) -> reproduce loss=nan on eval batches (single GPU V100 test)
- 2025-11-05: tried AWQ/GPTQ variants; FP32 and BF16 were stable, INT8 sometimes unstable. FP8 gave weird degredation but no NaNs initially.
- 2025-11-12: bisected code changes, suspected a fused kernel change in attention (PR GH#3421) that touched custom matmul kernel and attention fusion. Reverted locally -> fewer NaNs.

Commands / env used (notes to self):
- Repro (python script):
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python debug_quant_repro.py --model models/13b-int8 --batch 2 --seq_len 512 --fp16 

- Run with more debug:
  export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1
  export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
  python debug_quant_repro.py --model models/13b-int8 --profile

- Torch checks done:
  torch.isnan(out).any() -> True when NaN occurs
  torch.isnan(model.embed.weight).any() -> False (weights OK initially)
  torch.isinf(attn_scores).any() -> True sometimes

Observed errors / snippets:
- CUDA error on some runs: "RuntimeError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered" (stack points into fused attention kernel in serving-runtime).
- Downstream runtime: "ValueError: output contains NaN" in evaluation harness.
- Example printed from model logits: [-1.234e+30, NaN, NaN, -inf, 2.3e+02]
- Loss trace: loss = nan after 12 steps when using INT8; same config BF16 -> loss stable and matches baseline numbers.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Quantization scale collapse / zero scale for some channel -> division by zero during dequant -> inf/NaN. Especially for per-channel quantization with small groupsize.
2) Fused attention kernel bug interacting with int8 dequant path (scale ordering/residual scaling mismatch). Reverting kernel reduces frequency -> plausible.
3) Outlier activation values that are rare but cause overflow when reduced mantissa in FP8 or clipped dynamic range in INT8.
4) KV-cache or past-key-value accumulation overflow (scales not applied consistently across cached tensors).
5) Bitsandbytes/CUDA version mismatch: older bnb versions have known issues with group-wise quantization and certain cuBLASLt combos.

Experiments tried + results:
- Run in FP32 / BF16: stable -> suggests model weights and architecture not fundamentally broken.
- Re-run INT8 with larger calibration set (10k tokens instead of 512): still occasional NaNs but frequency reduced. Suggests calibration helps but not full fix.
- Change group_size from 128 -> 64 -> worse (more NaNs). Try group_size=1024 -> fewer NaNs but quality suffers.
- Switched to per-channel symmetric quantization (instead of per-tensor asymmetric): slightly better but still NaNs.
- Disabled fused attention (fallback to reference kernels) -> NaNs nearly disappear. Strong signal pointing to fused kernel interaction.
- Tried bitsandbytes 0.39 vs 0.37: 0.39 (newer) reduced occurrence but not eliminated.
- Ran with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 to get better stack traces -> points to serving-runtime fused matmul / attention path.

Diagnostic checks to run (next):
- Instrument dequant path: assert scales > 1e-12 before dividing; log channels with tiny scales.
- Reproduce minimal failing input and dump intermediate activations (pre-attn, attn_scores, softmax_input) to numpy to inspect numeric ranges.
- Run with clamp on attn_scores: torch.clamp(attn_scores, -50, 50) as quick mitigation to see if eliminates NaN.
- Add checks on KV cache writes: any NaN/infs immediately after write.
- Run the same INT8 model but with CPU fallback dequant path (if feasible) to isolate GPU kernel vs quantization data issue.

Potential quick mitigations for customers:
- Pin to BF16 variants for critical routes while we debug INT8.
- Serve int8 with fused attention disabled (slower but safer) where available. Provide a config flag in rollout.
- Increase calibration set and use outlier-aware quantization (clip outliers) in model build pipeline.

Longer-term fixes / investigations:
- Audit fused attention kernel codepaths for assumptions about data layout and scale application order. There may be a missing multiply-by-scale in the cached KV write path.
- Add unit tests that run quantized inference with synthetic outliers and assert no NaNs.
- Explore AWQ / GPTQ alternatives — some use re-scaling and outlier handling that seems more robust on our testbeds.
- Evaluate FP8 inference (on supported hardware) with careful block-level accumulation to avoid NaN. Early tests show FP8 reduces memory and keeps quality in some cases, but FP8 rounding behavior can still produce outliers that need clipping.

Notes from code inspection (rough):
- GH PR 3421 introduced a fused matmul + softmax + dropout kernel optimized for contiguous (N,C) layout and assumed pre-quant scales applied to data. If quantized path skips an expected reorder, scale defined per-channel might be applied to wrong axis.
- Also saw in kernels: a comment about "scale_inv" being computed as 1.0 / (scale + 1e-8) but in quant path a scale of exactly 0.0 can slip through due to int truncation -> leads to inf. Need to harden.

Temporary code checklist (TODO):
- [ ] Add guard to dequant: if scale < 1e-6 -> set to median non-zero scale or fallback value.
- [ ] Add assert / early fail for NaN in attention path and dump inputs to S3 with trace id.
- [ ] Roll out server config to prefer BF16 for high-priority customers (console flag).
- [ ] Create unit test for fused attention + INT8 with random outliers (GH issue created GH-4552).

Followups / comms:
- Pinged @Maya (SRE) in #serving-runtime about temporarily disabling fused attention for Canary hosts.
- Created JIRA INF-1287 to track the incident and follow-up remediation.
- Drafting a short note to CS/QA: suggest rerun regression with BF16 pinned and provide sample failing inputs.

Useful debugging commands / snippets:
- Dump activations (inside kernel wrapper):
  import numpy as np
  np.save(f"/tmp/dump_{trace_id}_pre_attn.npy", pre_attn.cpu().numpy())

- Quick clamp to test hypothesis:
  attn_scores = torch.clamp(attn_scores, -50.0, 50.0)

- Find tiny scales in quant params:
  scales = model.state_dict()['quant.scales']
  (scales == 0).sum(), scales.min(), scales.max()

- Local repro runner: debug_quant_repro.py (lightweight harness)
  - accepts flags: --model, --quant-backend (bnb/gptq/awq), --group-size, --calib-set, --disable-fused-attn

Notes to self about next experiments schedule:
- 1 day: add logging + clamp the dequant path and run full eval (overnight) to see if NaNs vanish.
- 2 day: add small unit test in CI that runs the quantized fused-attn path with injected outliers.
- 3 day: if fused kernel is root cause, propose a PR to either fix scale application or add a safe fallback for quantized inputs.

References / tickets: see linked_artifacts above.

Misc scratch thoughts:
- Could also be TF32 vs FP32 differences on Ampere architecture interacting with fused kernel math--worth trying disable tf32: torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False
- Customer impact prioritization: only routes with heavy batching (continuous batching) seen to trigger earlier; possible correlation with long context lengths (512+) -> floating accumulation longer -> larger dynamic ranges.

End of notes.

(Will convert into a tidy incident report once we have deterministic repro and a fix.)
